title: Day of Atonement
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2026-10-05

Opens [Sir 43](/bible/sirach/43) · [Gen 1](/bible/genesis/1) · [Exod 12](/bible/exodus/12) · [Exod 13](/bible/exodus/13) · [Lev 23](/bible/leviticus/23) · [Lev 16](/bible/leviticus/16) · [Exod 30](/bible/exodus/30) · [Isa 58](/bible/isaiah/58) · [Jonah 3](/bible/jonah/3) · [Acts 27](/bible/acts/27) · [Joel 2](/bible/joel/2) · [Prov 28](/bible/proverbs/28) · [Jude 1](/bible/jude/1) · [2 Pet 2](/bible/2-peter/2) · [Sir 6](/bible/sirach/6) · [1 Pet 2](/bible/1-peter/2) · and 12 more below
## Introduction *[[10:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=626s)]* All right. All right. All praises of the Lord. Happy day of atonement, y'all. Happy DOA. Some of y'all ain't prepared too well. That's why y'all sound tired like that. Some probably had crackers and that's it. Y'all going to suffer for 24 hours. *[[10:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=652s)]* But for your sakes, the class will not be that long. Normally on the day of atonement we don't have long, drawn out classes. So let's jump into it. Day of Atonement 2026. The class lays out the day from the law: the moon in her fulness as the sign of the feasts, the new moon of the seventh month, and the tenth day of that month as a Sabbath of rest and a holy convocation, kept evening to evening wherever Israel dwells. Isaiah 58 explains what "afflict your souls" means: to fast, with no eating and no drinking, and Paul kept the fast at sea. Then the teacher turns the day on the congregation: the day is self-examination, and a fast kept with bitterness, hatred and malice in the heart is wasted. He walks bitterness through three steps, fester, ferment and fragment, until the one who carries it separates himself from the assembly. The class closes on the atonement itself: the high priest went in once a year with the blood of others, Christ entered once with his own blood, so the animals are done away with, but Israel still keeps the feast days, the Day of Atonement included. ## Scriptures Opened **[Sirach 43:6-9](/bible/sirach/43#v6)** *[[11:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=675s)]* > [6](/bible/sirach/43#v6) He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. > > [7](/bible/sirach/43#v7) From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. > > [8](/bible/sirach/43#v8) The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven; > > [9](/bible/sirach/43#v9) The beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars, an ornament giving light in the highest places of the Lord. - The moon is a sign of feast. The word month comes from moon. - Decreasing in her perfection, because she starts off full and begins to decrease. So she is in her perfection when she is full. That is a designator for when the feast days are to be kept. - Increasing wonderfully in her changing: she goes from decreasing back to increasing until she is perfect again. An instrument of the armies above, meaning the angels. - Verse 1 all the way down talks about the rainbow, the sun, the moon, when they're bright and highest at their peak. It's referring to all the ornaments of heaven in their glory, in their perfection. The moon in her glory is the sign of feast, which is full. Not unseen. **[Genesis 1:14-16](/bible/genesis/1#v14)** *[[13:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=835s)]* > [14](/bible/genesis/1#v14) And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years: > > [15](/bible/genesis/1#v15) And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so. > > [16](/bible/genesis/1#v16) And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also. - For signs of the time, signs of the world, and for seasons, to determine the feast days that fall in their seasons. - The greater light to rule the day is the sun; the lesser light to rule the night is the moon. That also goes into stars, planets. **[Exodus 12:2](/bible/exodus/12#v2)** *[[15:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=914s)]* > [2](/bible/exodus/12#v2) This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you. - The first thing given to us was our new moon, because under Egypt they had a 10-day week. So the Lord had to let us know: this is the time when your month begins. **[Exodus 13:4](/bible/exodus/13#v4)** *[[15:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=947s)]* > [4](/bible/exodus/13#v4) This day came ye out in the month Abib. - That month is the first month of the year to us: Abib. That is late March to early April. Not January, not February. That's not the new year. In Babylon it was called Nisan. **[Leviticus 23:1-4](/bible/leviticus/23#v1)** *[[16:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=969s)]* > [1](/bible/leviticus/23#v1) And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, > > [2](/bible/leviticus/23#v2) Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts. > > [3](/bible/leviticus/23#v3) Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings. > > [4](/bible/leviticus/23#v4) These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons. - Concerning the feasts of the Lord: more than one. Holy convocations means holy gatherings, where you assemble yourselves together. To convoke means to come together. - Verse 2 is the introduction to the feasts. Verse 3 is the seventh day Sabbath, a weekly feast, a holy convocation. Wherever you dwell, in the land or outside the land, that is your Sabbath. - Verse 4 is something else: holy convocations, plural, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons. What do we use to determine the seasonal feast days? The moon. The full moon in her perfection. **[Leviticus 23:24](/bible/leviticus/23#v24)** *[[18:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=1118s)]* > [24](/bible/leviticus/23#v24) Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation. - The seventh month is the highest of the months. In the first day of the month shall ye have a Sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets. So the new moon is a Sabbath. - The new moon Sabbath and the seventh day Sabbath are not the same thing. There are two distinct Sabbaths: one monthly, and one weekly, which runs irrespective of the days of the months. **[Leviticus 23:27-32](/bible/leviticus/23#v27)** *[[19:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=1172s)]* > [27](/bible/leviticus/23#v27) Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord. > > [28](/bible/leviticus/23#v28) And ye shall do no work in that same day: for it is a day of atonement, to make an atonement for you before the Lord your God. > > [29](/bible/leviticus/23#v29) For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people. > > [30](/bible/leviticus/23#v30) And whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people. > > [31](/bible/leviticus/23#v31) Ye shall do no manner of work: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations in all your dwellings. > > [32](/bible/leviticus/23#v32) It shall be unto you a sabbath of rest, and ye shall afflict your souls: in the ninth day of the month at even, from even unto even, shall ye celebrate your sabbath. - The first day of the seventh month is the new moon, the blowing of trumpets. The tenth day of it is a day of atonement. - Ye shall afflict your souls. That's not clarified here. We got to go somewhere else to explain what that means. - Offer an offering made by fire: during Moses' times, on the day of atonement, we had to afflict our souls and then offer up sacrifices. Keep that in mind. It's very important. - Ye shall do no work in that same day, because it's a Sabbath. Cut off and destroy are synonymous: cut off means to kill. - A statute forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings: whether in Jerusalem or outside Jerusalem. Are we still generating? Yes. So we're still to do it. - Honor the Sabbath day and keep it holy: it's not just one. It's multiple Sabbaths, depending on what feast day it is. Day of atonement falls under that as well. - The ninth day of the month at even is the tenth day. From evening to evening, not day to day. That's how we counted our days. Day begins at night and ends at night. Those that believed there was a sunrise Sabbath, where are they today? Going with the wind, eating chicken and pork in the world. **[Leviticus 16:29-34](/bible/leviticus/16#v29)** *[[23:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=1393s)]* > [29](/bible/leviticus/16#v29) And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you: > > [30](/bible/leviticus/16#v30) For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the Lord. > > [31](/bible/leviticus/16#v31) It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever. > > [32](/bible/leviticus/16#v32) And the priest, whom he shall anoint, and whom he shall consecrate to minister in the priest’s office in his father’s stead, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen clothes, even the holy garments: > > [33](/bible/leviticus/16#v33) And he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make an atonement for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar, and he shall make an atonement for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation. > > [34](/bible/leviticus/16#v34) And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. And he did as the Lord commanded Moses. - Whether it be one of your own country or a stranger: the priest makes the atonement for you, to cleanse you, that you may be clean from all your sins before the Lord. - Shall the priest make an atonement for you: remember earlier I said you offer sacrifices. - This shall be an everlasting statute, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. So day of atonement is done once a year. **[Exodus 30:10](/bible/exodus/30#v10)** *[[25:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=1517s)]* > [10](/bible/exodus/30#v10) And Aaron shall make an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements: once in the year shall he make atonement upon it throughout your generations: it is most holy unto the Lord. - Once in a year, with the blood of the sin offering of atonements. **[Isaiah 58:3-13](/bible/isaiah/58#v3)** *[[26:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=1575s)]* > [3](/bible/isaiah/58#v3) Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge? Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours. > > [4](/bible/isaiah/58#v4) Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high. > > [5](/bible/isaiah/58#v5) Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the Lord? > > [6](/bible/isaiah/58#v6) Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? > > [7](/bible/isaiah/58#v7) Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh? > > [8](/bible/isaiah/58#v8) Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the Lord shall be thy rereward. > > [9](/bible/isaiah/58#v9) Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity; > > [10](/bible/isaiah/58#v10) And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noonday: > > [11](/bible/isaiah/58#v11) And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not. > > [12](/bible/isaiah/58#v12) And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in. > > [13](/bible/isaiah/58#v13) If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: - Some of y'all are wondering, what does afflict your soul mean? Hit yourself in the face? No, that's not what it means. Wherefore have we fasted? Wherefore have we afflicted our soul? Fasting and affliction of soul are the same thing. The prophets explain, but Moses does not. - In the day of your fast ye find pleasure and exact all your labours: Israel did what they wanted to do while fasting, doing business, making their money, when the scripture says specifically it is a Sabbath, no work. So the Most High was not listening to them at all. - Ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: they were fighting among themselves, debating back and forth, getting into confrontations. You can't fast how you've been doing it. The fasting is a waste of time. I'm not listening to that. - Is not this the fast that I have chosen? We have many fasts, but the Bible says the fast is the day of atonement. To loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens: that's to cleanse you of all your sins. - Deal thy bread to the hungry, cover the naked, hide not thyself from thine own flesh: look out for each other, love your neighbor as yourself, your own people. We were doing all kinds of evil and yet fasting anyway. - Then shall thy light break forth: so when you stop doing those things, then I'll listen to you. The putting forth of the finger is the debating, the arguing, the confrontations. - They that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: return to our land again. It's a prophecy, if we do these things right. - Turn away thy foot from the Sabbath: the fast in verse 6, the day of atonement. From doing thy pleasure: the pleasure back in verse 3, the business, the fighting, arguing, debating, making money, laboring. - Not finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: doing what you want to do, fasting how you want to fast. A water fast, a juice fast? No. Fast means no nothing. No eating, drinking, nothing. **[Jonah 3:5,7](/bible/jonah/3#v5)** *[[31:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=1916s)]* > [5](/bible/jonah/3#v5) So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. > > [7](/bible/jonah/3#v7) And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water: - Let's see what fasting is. Let neither man nor beast taste anything. Let them not feed nor drink water. No eating, no drinking, nothing at all. 24 hours, evening to evening. - You're not going to die. You'll be just fine once a year. Taste nothing: no brushing of the teeth. Don't try to be slick, take a shower and open your mouth. Taste nothing. **[Acts 27:6,9](/bible/acts/27#v6)** *[[33:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=2028s)]* > [6](/bible/acts/27#v6) And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein. > > [9](/bible/acts/27#v9) Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them, - Isaiah 58 mentioned the fast. Let's see if Paul kept the fast. Christianity says in the New Testament that's done away with. - The ship of Alexandria, Egypt, sailing into Italy, to Rome. So when Paul was fasting, where was he? On a boat, fasting on the day of atonement. He was not in Jerusalem. He was sailing, traveling during this time. - The reference by the fast gives Leviticus 23:27-29: the fast was on the tenth day of the seventh month. That is the day of atonement, in which the priest would offer sacrifices for us once a year. But once Christ died on that cross, Paul could do it without the sacrificing, because Christ was that sacrifice. **[Joel 2:12-13](/bible/joel/2#v12)** *[[35:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=2132s)]* > [12](/bible/joel/2#v12) Therefore also now, saith the Lord, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: > > [13](/bible/joel/2#v13) And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil. - With fasting, with weeping, with mourning: repentance, sincere remorse. - Rend your heart and not your garments. Whenever Israel went through an affliction or a sadness, we would rip our clothes. He says rend your mind: repent. Ripping your clothes don't mean a thing to me. You got to fast and be sincere about it. **[Proverbs 28:13](/bible/proverbs/28#v13)** *[[36:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=2214s)]* > [13](/bible/proverbs/28#v13) He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy. - The atonement is a time of self-reflection. Once a year you examine your sins, what you've done. Some of you battling hatred, anger, fornication, jealousy, envy. Bitterness, that's a big one in here. - You can't hide those things. They eventually leak out of you over time. They corrupt you. - An author mentioned three Fs, and it's not my quote: whatever you choose not to let go, it festers, it ferments, and it becomes fragmented. - Fester: for a negative feeling or a bad situation to grow worse over time because it is ignored. It grows, it spreads, and you refuse to acknowledge it. - Ferment: to be in a state of agitation; turmoil, unrest, upheaval. First it festers, then you undergo change. You see it in the person's face, their countenance changes, they act different, they speak different, they isolate themselves. At that point you and Satan are best friends. Everybody becomes the bad guy, and only you see the spirit. - But whoso confesseth: if you got a problem, you speak on it. You don't want to speak on it, it will fester, and it will ferment. - Fragment: a small piece that has broken off, or separated from a whole. **[Jude 1:19-20](/bible/jude/1#v19)** *[[45:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=2730s)]* > [19](/bible/jude/1#v19) These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit. > > [20](/bible/jude/1#v20) But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, - Separate themselves: that's the fragment. Sensual: emotional. Having not the Spirit. - Building up yourselves: I can't be in your brain to tell you what to do. You know if you're angry and bitter and hateful and sad or depressed. That's on you. You have to speak on that. Those of y'all who do not grow worse and worse over time. - Now they're in the back of the class. Everyone's hanging out, and you leave. Shalom y'all. You got work tomorrow? Nah. That's fragmentation. Fester, ferment, fragment: the three Fs. **[2 Peter 2:10](/bible/2-peter/2#v10)** *[[45:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=2759s)]* > [10](/bible/2-peter/2#v10) But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities. - Peter says the same thing. That's the fragmentation. Over time you become a Judas, untrustworthy. Everyone becomes the enemy. Now you doing videos, why I left. It's downhill from there. Now you're eating chicken nuggets on Passover. There's steps to it. **[Sirach 6:1-7,13](/bible/sirach/6#v1)** *[[48:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=2931s)]* > [1](/bible/sirach/6#v1) Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby thou shalt inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that hath a double tongue. > > [2](/bible/sirach/6#v2) Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart; that thy soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone. > > [3](/bible/sirach/6#v3) Thou shalt eat up thy leaves, and lose thy fruit, and leave thyself as a dry tree. > > [4](/bible/sirach/6#v4) A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies. > > [5](/bible/sirach/6#v5) Sweet language will multiply friends: and a fairspeaking tongue will increase kind greetings. > > [6](/bible/sirach/6#v6) Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand. > > [7](/bible/sirach/6#v7) If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him. > > [13](/bible/sirach/6#v13) Separate thyself from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends. - You watch the nature channel: there's the herd, and there's that one that wanders off. Fragmentation. - Instead of a friend become not an enemy, for thereby thou shalt inherit an ill name: you become untrustworthy. We can't trust you. We want to bring so and so along with us? Nah, he can stay back. - A sinner that hath a double tongue: in one breath, God bless, how you doing, brother; in the back of your mind, I can't stand him. That's double tongued, because of that festering, that fermenting and that fragmentation. - Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart: verse 2 is what took place in verse 1 for you to become the enemy in the first place. You've taken counsel from your own mind, your feelings. Sensual goes back to being emotional. - Torn in pieces as a bull straying alone: torn to pieces by the lion, and the lion in the Bible is the devil. Don't stray from the herd. Don't fragment. - Thou shalt eat up thy leaves: over time you will lose your understanding. Whatever you think you know, you will forget. - Laughed to scorn of his enemies: remember that dude that used to be with us? He was a captain of so and so. Sunrise Sabbath. Where he at now? Now you're a story to tell, because you turned against brothers that looked out for you and your family. - Have but one counsellor of a thousand: you ain't got to tell the whole world you're going through something. Talk to someone. If you say, I talk to the Bible, I talk to the law, you are extolling yourself in your own mind, verse 2. - Separate thyself from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends: you see a brother doing verses 1 through 4, you keep a distance. Be very mindful of your friends and how they act. They might become verses 1 through 4 because of that bitterness in them. **[1 Peter 2:1-2](/bible/1-peter/2#v1)** *[[55:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=3319s)]* > [1](/bible/1-peter/2#v1) Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, > > [2](/bible/1-peter/2#v2) As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby: - Malice: the intention or desire to cause harm, pain or distress to another person. That's internal. Some people feel good doing that and have joy in hurting people. - Even certain Israelite camps have the same spirit: look for a way to destroy and discredit us. We've done nothing to you at all. That is an evil spirit. - Malevolent: having or showing a strong, lasting wish to do evil. That's the ferment. Malignant, tending to produce death, goes back to fermentation; vindictive goes into the fragmentation. I ain't coming to the school that day, I'mma stay home and watch online. - The Bishop mentions all the time having a circle you can trust. When brothers act weird within the circle, it's noticeable. Rather than say something, he keeps it to himself, and over time shows resentment. - Envies is secret hatred. You lay these things aside, and then you grow. Otherwise you become spiritually stillborn, sitting in class, no notes being taken, just looking around mad. **[Ephesians 4:31-32](/bible/ephesians/4#v31)** *[[1:00:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDdyWiftNlk&t=3631s)]* > [31](/bible/ephesians/4#v31) Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: > > [32](/bible/ephesians/4#v32) And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you. - Paul saying the same exact thing Peter said. Otherwise you'll grow the wrong way, to the left hand side of the Lord, not the right. - That also turns into Sabbath sickness: you show up on the feast days and outings, but Sabbath, I'm sick. Because there's a festering, fermentation or fragmentation going on. - I despise cliques. A brother who has an evil spirit feels comfortable coming to you about somebody else. Why is that brother coming to you? Something might be in you also. That's the spirit of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. - Bitterness is the first word he mentions. Clamour is murmuring. It's the same thing as Isaiah 58: the putting forth of the finger, the wickedness, your pleasure.
